Combined Depth Cueing and Shading (Reversed Order) is a frequency-domain volume rendering technique that combines directional shading and depth cueing by reversing their standard physical order of operations to enable a single composite filter application [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that 'Combined Depth Cueing and Shading (Reversed Order)' is a frequency-domain volume rendering technique that combines directional shading and depth cueing by reversing their standard physical order to enable a single composite filter application. Source [S1] and [S2] explicitly confirm: 1) The standard physical order requires shading first then depth cueing, which prevents the use of the composite filter H' and requires two convolutions. 2) Reversing the order (depth cueing first, then shading) allows the use of the single composite filter H' to perform interpolation and depth cueing at once. 3) This reversal introduces an error term that can be adjusted or is zero under specific conditions (L perpendicular to V). Thus, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
